acme_integ: Hey @elena_support — we flipped structured_output.json_mode to "strict" and now our invoice endpoint started returning parse failures. Worked fine before. sample request + model response below, please advise.

elena_support: can you paste the minimal request and the raw model response? also send request_id if you have it. which model/version?

acme_integ: request_id=req_20250315_88fa
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '
{
  "model": "rwd-infer-1",
  "structured_output": {
    "json_mode": "strict",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "amount_cents": {"type": "integer"},
        "paid": {"type": "boolean"},
        "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["PAID", "PENDING", "VOID"]}
      },
      "required": ["amount_cents", "paid", "status"]
    }
  }
}'

Model returned (raw):
{
  "amount_cents": "1200",
  "paid": null,
  "status": "paid"
}

We get an API error: "parse_failure: schema mismatch: expected boolean for field 'paid' but got null (strict mode)" and also enum fails on "paid" vs "PAID". Previously model produced booleans and uppercase enums.

ops-bot: [ingest] parse_failure logged for req_20250315_88fa, rule=strict_json_validation, node=rt-05

sam_engineer: thanks for the repro — two things happening: 1) model emitted "amount_cents" as a string ("1200") not integer, 2) emitted null for a boolean field and lowercased enum. In strict mode we currently treat null as invalid for booleans and do exact enum matching.

sam_engineer: quick repro you can try to confirm behavior locally: set "structured_output.json_mode" to "strict" and add "request_debug": true. Example minimal body we used above reproduces it.

sam_engineer: short-term workarounds: 1) set "json_mode": "permissive" or 2) postprocess the model output: coerce numeric-strings -> ints and map lowercase enums to canonical case, and treat nulls for booleans as false if that matches your domain. Example mapping: `status = status.upper()` and `paid = bool(paid) if paid is not None else False`.

acme_integ: is there a recommended config flag to allow strings-for-numbers or null-for-bools instead of turning off strict entirely? toggling to permissive might hide other regressions for us.

elena_support: good question. we don't have a per-field coercion toggle exposed in the public API yet. i'll escalate to eng-ml and product — past customers have asked for "coerce_types" or "enum_case_insensitive" flags.

sam_engineer: opened internal ticket INC-8792 with the model team and attached your sample. Plan: add a temporary tolerant parser that, when enabled, will coerce numeric strings -> numbers and allow boolean-null collapse (configurable), plus an enum_case_insensitive option. ETA TBD but we'll post updates in this thread.

acme_integ: thanks. one more data point — we saw this only when the prompt included an example with "paid": "false" (string). seems like the model copied the type from the prompt.

sam_engineer: yep that can happen — model can learn type signals from few-shot examples. short-term, ensure examples match target types (use literal `true`/`false` and uppercase enums). we'll follow up on a runtime-side fix.

acme_integ: ok will try updating examples and toggling permissive while you folks patch. appreciate the quick response :thumbsup:

elena_support: thanks — we'll keep this open and update when INC-8792 has progress. please reply here after you confirm whether the example-change fixes it.
